hints: Look carefully at the two different functional groups in strobilurin, the ester group and the three C=C double bonds.
Warm aqueous sulfuric acid hydrolyses the methyl ester $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ to a carboxylic acid $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, while the alkenes survive this step.
Hydrogen with nickel catalyst then saturates every C=C to C-C but leaves the carboxylic acid unchanged, so track what the carbon skeleton should look like.
walkthrough:
**Spot the reactive groups in strobilurin**

Think like a detective. The molecule has one methyl ester, $\text{-CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, and three alkene $\text{C=C}$ bonds in the chain. R and R' are inert, so we can ignore them.

Key groups:
$$\text{R-CH=CH-CH=C(CH}_3\text{)-C(CO}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)=CH-R'}$$

**First reaction: acid hydrolysis to make X**

Warming with aqueous $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is classic acid hydrolysis of an ester. Water splits the ester into a carboxylic acid and methanol.

$$\text{R'CO}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{warm dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{R'CO}_2\text{H} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$$
So compound X still has the three C=C bonds, but now has $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ instead of $\text{-CO}_2\text{CH}_3$.

**Second reaction: catalytic hydrogenation to make Y**

Hydrogen with Ni catalyst adds $\text{H}_2$ across each $\text{C=C}$ to give $\text{C-C}$. It is a powerful reducer for alkenes but it does not reduce carboxylic acids under these conditions.

$$\text{C=C} + \text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni}} \text{CH-CH}$$
So all three double bonds become single bonds, giving a fully saturated chain: $\text{R-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH(CO}_2\text{H)-CH}_2\text{-R'}$. This matches the saturated carboxylic acid structure.

options.A: Correct. It shows the hydrolysed acid $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ and a fully saturated carbon chain. All three C=C bonds have been hydrogenated to C-C, while R, R' and the methyl branch are unchanged.
options.B: Incorrect. This shows $\text{CH(OH)(OCH}_3\text{)}$ instead of a carbonyl group. Warm aqueous acid hydrolyses the ester fully to $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ plus methanol, it does not stop at a hemiacetal type structure, and H2/Ni does not create this group.
options.C: Incorrect. This shows a primary alcohol $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ where the acid should be. Students choosing this think H2/Ni reduces the carboxylic acid, but Ni-catalysed hydrogenation reduces C=C only, not $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ to $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.
options.D: Incorrect. This shows extra OH groups added across the double bonds. That is the trap of acid-catalysed hydration of alkenes to alcohols, but the second step here is hydrogenation with H2/Ni which adds H atoms, not OH groups, to give alkanes.
